LESSON: PERCUSSION MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: CREATING AND EXECUTING Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Le
Topic 1.1: Percussion Musical Instruments

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Percussion Musical Instruments. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is the importance of percussion instruments from different communities in Kenya?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify indigenous percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities
2. classify indigenous Kenyan percussion musical instruments, as melodic or non-melodic
3. discuss the function(s) of parts of a percussion musical instrument
4. create tonal value on a drawing of a percussion

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PERCUSSION MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Percussion Musical Instruments helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: PERCUSSION MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS
Study Percussion Musical Instruments like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify indigenous percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities

What this means
In this part you learn to identify indigenous percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify indigenous percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Percussion Musical Instruments” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify indigenous percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Classify indigenous Kenyan percussion musical instruments, as melodic or non-melodic

What this means
In this part you learn to classify indigenous Kenyan percussion musical instruments, as melodic or non-melodic. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: classify indigenous Kenyan percussion musical instruments, as melodic or non-melodic.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Percussion Musical Instruments in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can classify indigenous Kenyan percussion musical instruments, as melodic or non-melodic. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Discuss the function(s) of parts of a percussion musical instrument

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss the function(s) of parts of a percussion musical instrument. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss the function(s) of parts of a percussion musical instrument.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss the function(s) of parts of a percussion musical instrument. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Create tonal value on a drawing of a percussion

What this means
In this part you learn to create tonal value on a drawing of a percussion. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create tonal value on a drawing of a percussion.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Percussion Musical Instruments” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create tonal value on a drawing of a percussion. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Percussion Musical Instruments is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Percussion Musical Instruments” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify indigenous percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Percussion Musical Instruments in your own words. (skill: classify indigenous Kenyan percussion musical instruments, as melodic or non-melodic)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: discuss the function(s) of parts of a percussion musical instrument)

Example 4: Show how “Percussion Musical Instruments” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: create tonal value on a drawing of a percussion)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Percussion Musical Instruments to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify indigenous percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities.
3. Practise this skill: classify indigenous Kenyan percussion musical instruments, as melodic or non-melodic.
4. Practise this skill: discuss the function(s) of parts of a percussion musical instrument.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Percussion Musical Instruments from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Percussion Musical Instruments: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Percussion Musical Instruments?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is the importance of percussion instruments from different communities in Kenya?
2. How is tonal variation created in a drawing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Percussion Musical Instruments means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify indigenous percussion musical instruments from different Kenyan communities.
5. Be able to: classify indigenous Kenyan percussion musical instruments, as melodic or non-melodic.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
